title: Monitoring and Alerting for Dead-Letter Queues
description: Instrument DLQs with metrics, dashboards, and alerts so failed messages are visible, actionable, and resolved before they become incidents.

data.text: A DLQ without monitoring is a black hole. Messages enter silently, and unless someone checks the queue depth regularly, failures go unnoticed until users report missing data. Effective DLQ monitoring surfaces volume trends, processing lag, and unusual error patterns so teams can respond before data loss accumulates.

data.title: Essential DLQ Metrics
items: DLQ depth: number of messages currently in the DLQ; sudden growth signals a processing failure
Main queue depth: a rising main queue with a flat DLQ can indicate consumers are stuck rather than failing
Message age in DLQ: how long messages have been sitting unprocessed; old messages need urgent attention
Processing rate: messages moved from DLQ back to the main queue per hour; measures recovery speed
Retry rate: messages retried before reaching the DLQ; spikes may indicate a downstream outage

data.text: Cloud providers expose these metrics natively. Amazon CloudWatch publishes ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible for SQS queues. Azure Monitor surfaces dead-letter message count for Service Bus. For on-premises RabbitMQ, use the management plugin or Prometheus exporters to scrape queue metrics.

Alerts should be actionable and tiered. A low-severity alert warns when DLQ depth exceeds a soft threshold, such as 100 messages. A high-severity alert fires when depth exceeds a hard threshold or when messages remain in the DLQ longer than the service-level objective, such as 4 hours.

data.title: Alert Fatigue Warning
data.text: Avoid paging on-call engineers for small DLQ depth changes. Page only when the condition threatens data loss or downstream SLA.

data.title: CloudWatch Alarm for SQS DLQ Depth (TypeScript CDK)
data.content: The AWS CDK lets you declare alarms that watch DLQ metrics and notify an SNS topic.

items.question: What is the difference between DLQ depth and main queue depth?
items.answer: Main queue depth tracks unprocessed work waiting for consumers. DLQ depth tracks failed work that cannot be processed without intervention. Both are important but signal different problems.

items.question: Should I use a log or a metrics system for DLQ monitoring?
items.answer: Use both. Metrics detect trends and trigger alerts. Logs provide context for root cause analysis. Metrics tell you something is wrong; logs explain why.

items.question: How often should I review DLQ dashboards?
items.answer: Automated alerts should catch spikes. A weekly dashboard review is usually enough for healthy queues. Increase review frequency if your error rate is above normal.
